title: Unicellular and Multicellular Organisms
subject: Biology
objective: An amoeba is one cell; you are about 37 trillion. In one, a single cell does everything; in the other, cells share the work.

fill.q: An organism made of a single cell is called ____.
In multicellular organisms different cells do different jobs: this is called division of ____.
Every multicellular organism starts as a single cell called the ____.

tf.q: A unicellular organism carries out all life processes in one cell.
Nerve cells and muscle cells have the same shape and job.
tf.explain: They are specialised for different jobs.

ar.a: Multicellular organisms show division of labour.
ar.r: Different cells in them are specialised for different jobs.

ar.a: Amoeba needs separate cells for digestion and movement.
ar.explain: A is false: its one cell does every job; R is true.

mcq.q: Which cell carries oxygen in humans?

short.q: Compare unicellular and multicellular organisms with examples.
short.solution: Unicellular: one cell does all life processes (Amoeba, bacteria). Multicellular: many cells with division of labour (plants, animals, humans).

short.q: Why do multicellular organisms need division of labour?
short.solution: With many cells, different groups specialise (muscle for movement, nerve for signals), so the body works efficiently.

right: First cell of a multicellular organism
match.explain: Size and complexity come from many specialised cells.
